subject: general
question: I bought two pendants for ₹1,200. I sold the first one at a loss of 10% and the second at a gain of 14%. If, on the whole I made neither a loss nor a gain, find the cost price (in ₹) of the first pendant.
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Using the Alligation Method on Profit & Loss percentages:

Loss on 1st = −10%, Gain on 2nd = +14%, Net = 0%

Ratio of Cost Prices = (14 − 0) : (0 − (−10)) = 14 : 10 = 7 : 5

Total ratio parts = 7 + 5 = 12 parts

CP of 1st Pendant = (7 / 12) × 1200 = 700

**∴ The correct answer is ₹700.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Total Cost Price of two pendants = ₹1,200

Loss on 1st Pendant = 10%

Gain on 2nd Pendant = 14%

Overall transaction yields neither loss nor gain (Net = 0).

**Calculations:**

⇒ Since there is neither loss nor gain, the absolute loss on the first item is equal to the absolute gain on the second item.

⇒ 10% of CP₁ = 14% of CP₂

⇒ 10 × CP₁ = 14 × CP₂

⇒ CP₁ / CP₂ = 14 / 10

⇒ CP₁ : CP₂ = 7 : 5

⇒ Let CP₁ = 7x and CP₂ = 5x

⇒ Total Cost Price = 7x + 5x = 12x

⇒ 12x = 1200

⇒ x = 100

⇒ Cost Price of 1st Pendant (CP₁) = 7 × 100 = 700

**∴ The correct answer is ₹700.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Alligation in Profit & Loss

When two items are sold at varying profit/loss percentages, alligation yields the ratio of their Cost Prices: (P₂ − Net) : (Net − P₁).

No Profit No Loss Principle

When an overall transaction yields zero net change, the absolute numerical value of the loss on one part perfectly offsets the absolute gain on the other, establishing a direct inverse ratio of their rates.

Cost Price from Ratios

If Total CP = T, and CP₁ : CP₂ = a : b, then CP₁ = T × [a / (a + b)] and CP₂ = T × [b / (a + b)].
